label: lem:eig-root-of-unity
title: Eigenvalues of a finite-order endomorphism are $n$-th roots of unity
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{C}$, let $n : \mathbb{N}$ with $n \neq 0$ (equivalently $0 < n$), and let $f : V \to_{\ell} V$ be an endomorphism with $f^n = \mathrm{id}_V$.  Then for every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $f$, $\lambda^n = 1$.
proof: Let $v \neq 0$ be an eigenvector for $\lambda$.  By \verb|Module.End.HasEigenvalue.pow|, $f^n$ has eigenvalue $\lambda^n$ on the same eigenvector $v$.  But $f^n = \mathrm{id}_V$ has only the eigenvalue $1$ on any nonzero vector.  More concretely: unfolding the definition of an eigenvector gives $f^n v = \lambda^n \cdot v$; on the other hand $f^n v = v$, so $\lambda^n v = v$, i.e.\ $(\lambda^n - 1) \cdot v = 0$, and since $v \neq 0$ over a field this forces $\lambda^n = 1$.
